items.label: GS Renderer (restart)
items.info: Vulkan renders the GS on the GPU. OpenGL does the same through the frontend's GL context, for devices with no usable Vulkan driver. Software renders on the CPU and presents through the same shared context.

items.label: Internal Resolution
items.info: Renders the PS2 output at a multiple of native resolution. The output canvas follows this size.

items.label: Aspect Ratio
items.info: Display aspect ratio. 16:9 is intended for games with widescreen patches or native widescreen modes.

items.label: Deinterlacing
items.info: How interlaced (480i/576i) output is turned into a full frame. Automatic picks per game; Bob is fast, Adaptive is highest quality; Off shows the raw field.

items.label: No-Interlacing Patches (restart)
items.info: Patches supported games to render progressive instead of interlaced — sharper than any deinterlacer.

items.label: Widescreen Patches (restart)
items.info: Patches supported games to render 16:9. Set Aspect Ratio to 16:9 alongside this.

items.label: Blending Accuracy
items.info: How accurately PS2 framebuffer blending is emulated on the GPU. Lower levels are faster; raise it only for games with visible blending artifacts.

items.label: Dithering
items.info: Unscaled replicates PS2 dithering; Off can reduce banding artifacts at higher internal resolutions.

items.label: FXAA
items.info: Cheap post-process anti-aliasing.

items.label: Texture Filtering
items.info: Bilinear (PS2) filters as the game requests. Forced filters everything, which smooths textures but can blur 2D elements; the sprite-excluding variant protects UI sprites.

items.label: Anisotropic Filtering
items.info: Sharpens textures viewed at an angle. Cheap on the GPU, but can cause artifacts in games that rely on point sampling.

items.label: Software Renderer Threads
items.info: Worker threads for the Software renderer (in addition to the GS thread). No effect on Vulkan.

items.label: Show FPS
items.info: Draws the internal framerate on screen.

sections.label: Performance
sections.info: Speed hacks trading accuracy for framerate.

items.label: EE Cycle Rate
items.info: Underclocks or overclocks the emulated Emotion Engine. Below 100% speeds up emulation but can cause stutter or breakage; above 100% can smooth out games with internal slowdown.

items.label: EE Cycle Skip
items.info: Makes the emulated EE skip cycles. Helps games with obvious VU-driven slowdown; can cause false FPS readings and breakage.

items.label: Hardware Download Mode
items.info: How GS-to-EE readbacks are handled. Accurate is correct but expensive on mobile GPUs; Disable Readbacks skips the data copy, Unsynchronized doesn't wait for the GPU, Disabled ignores the transfer entirely. Anything but Accurate can break effects that read the framebuffer.

items.label: MTVU (Multi-Threaded VU1)
items.info: Runs VU1 on its own thread. Large speedup on multi-core CPUs; a small number of games hang with it.

items.label: Instant VU1
items.info: Runs VU1 programs to completion instantly instead of interleaving with the EE. Fast and safe for most games.

items.label: BIOS (restart)
items.info: Which BIOS image from <system>/pcsx2/bios to boot. Auto picks the first valid image.

items.label: Fast Boot
items.info: Skips the BIOS boot animation.

items.label: Enable Cheats
items.info: Loads .pnach cheat files from <system>/pcsx2/cheats for the running game.
